messages:
Ravi (Eng): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A on security/privacy. Couple of customers asked about long-term audit log retention and whether Redwood supports pushing logs to their SIEM. Anyone have the canonical answer we can share?

Nina (Security): Yes — supported. Defaults: Hosted = 90d, Dedicated = 1y. Private deployments are configurable; weve implemented 3-7+ year retention for enterprise, but it requires sizing and contract terms. Exports: S3-compatible targets, syslog over VPC, and Kafka endpoints are supported. We'll publish a short FAQ.

Liam (Product): Note for customers: exporting to customer-managed storage may incur transfer/egress costs. We recommend lifecycle policies (tiering -> glacier) for multi-year retention. Console path: Settings > Audit Logs > Export.

Zoe (Privacy): Reminder: retention beyond 12 months can trigger region-specific privacy reviews. If customer is in EU/UK/CN we need to confirm lawful basis and DSAR handling. Also: searching and redacting records in archived stores needs documented procedures. I'll draft guidance.

Chris (SRE): Technical note: logs are append-only and HMAC-signed at ingestion; chain metadata retained for tamper-evidence. Key rotation for signing is monthly by default. For BYOK, we support customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault) and can integrate with on-prem HSM via mTLS.

Ravi (Eng): For BYOK/HSM, does Redwood ever touch plaintext key material?

Nina (Security): No. In BYOK mode we store key references and grants only. For AWS KMS we rely on grants; for on-prem HSM we call a signing proxy. We never store raw key bytes.

Liam (Product): Roadmap update: UI for key lifecycle (rotate/revoke/audit) and a rotation events audit view planned for Q4. Internal beta in ~8-12 weeks.

Ravi (Eng): Can we include Private deployments in SOC 2 scope? Customer asked if their VPC/Private cluster could be covered by our attestation.

Nina (Security): Our SOC 2 covers Redwood control plane and managed infra. Private is shared-responsibility: we provide control-plane controls and artifacts; customer owns infra/network/physical controls. We provide a SOC2 mapping pack (evidence templates + control mappings) to help customers and auditors. For on-prem air-gapped setups we can provide tailored readiness letters but cannot extend our SOC2 to their machines without audit engagement.

Zoe (Privacy): If they require combined ISO/SOC scope, we can map artifacts to ISO controls but some controls will remain with customer. Additional short audits often required for combined scope.

Chris (SRE): Practical: when exporting to customer S3, decide who manages retention lifecycle. Both patterns supported: Redwood-managed lifecycle or customer-managed bucket lifecycle. For legal holds, recommend customer-managed.

Ravi (Eng): Any CLI example to enable S3 export quickly?

Nina (Security): Example: 
```
redwoodctl logs export enable --deployment dp-abc123 --target s3://corp-audit --format json --encrypt --kms arn:aws:kms:region:acct:key/xyz
```
Make sure VPC endpoints and IAM grants are configured first. Full flags in docs.

Liam (Product): Also we're prototyping a sidecar shipper for Private so ops teams don't have to run fluentd themselves. Target for next quarter.

Ravi (Eng): One last thing: customer wants proof of key rotation (who/when). Is that surfaced?

Nina (Security): Yes. Rotation events are logged (actor, timestamp, operation). For BYOK we record key-reference changes. We can also produce signed rotation event artifacts for audits on request.

Zoe (Privacy): Action: I'll write DSAR guidance for long-retention logs (search/remove requests).

Chris (SRE): Action items: Nina to publish audit-export FAQ + how-to; Liam to add BYOK/UI timeline to roadmap; Chris to estimate storage costs for multi-year retention and post numbers.

ops-bot: Ticket created: #TICKET-4217 "post-allhands-audit-log-guidance" assigned to Nina (Security) due 2025-01-22.

Nina (Security): Thanks all  If anyone wants to pair on the BYOK HSM integration design, ping me and well set a short sync.
